lead: Apollo's Torsten Slok says AI has returned zero financial payoff outside tech, and the market's answer arrives the same morning: Aramco buys into Humain for $2.6B and three more rounds close. Meanwhile Postgres slips a release on LLM-found bugs, and fake AI wikis colonize the search results.

sections.title: The payoff question
sections.intro: Apollo's chief economist counts the S&P 493's margins and finds AI has paid corporate America outside tech exactly nothing - and Kioxia's 15% drop shows how jumpy the demand story has become.

sections.title: The discipline holds
sections.intro: An engineer's case for keeping decisions reviewable while agents implement, and Postgres 19 slipping because LLMs find bugs faster than committers can fix them.

sections.title: The workbench
sections.intro: One developer's confession: he turned ordinary ChatGPT chats into a multi-agent dev shop over MCP, and OpenAI's usage merger is closing the loophole.

sections.title: The money keeps moving
sections.intro: Aramco takes 49% of Humain for $2.6B, Broccoli AI banks $52M for answering plumbers' phones, Hex raises $100M for an agent-ready rebuild, and Hyperbolic adds $30M for neocloud compute.

sections.title: Slop in the search results
sections.intro: Eurogamer finds AI-generated fake wikis outranking real ones for indie games - invented companions, bounced contact addresses, and publishers playing whack-a-mole.

sections.title: The policy blitz
sections.intro: Axios: OpenAI readies a post-midterms push for mandatory AI 'speed limits' and a friendlier name for its data centers.

sections.title: Measuring the frontier
sections.intro: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx: eleven high-ROI domains, safety classifiers and all - and the best model on Earth scores 12%.

sections.title: The bill for the troves
sections.intro: Doctorow's 'Autodoxing': twenty-five years of surveillance policy was foreseen, and AI-era identification is collecting on it.

sections.title: The verticals collect
sections.intro: Vera Health banks $28.5M for evidence-first clinical search, Midstream $20M for hospital revenue recovery, Casap $56M for dispute automation, and Bites $40M for frontline training.

sections.title: The manifesto itself
sections.intro: Proton publishes the AI engineering manifesto behind the week's 'loser thinking' storm - the reactions are in yesterday's digest.

sections.title: The intrusion post-mortem
sections.intro: Microsoft traces a malicious Claude Code Cursor-extension incident from Teams impersonation to certificate-services abuse.

sections.title: Export controls, mirrored
sections.intro: China issues its first frontier-AI export controls - Mofcom Announcement No. 48 answers the American playbook.

sections.title: Seoul doubles down
sections.intro: President Lee vows $15.97B for AI, chips and data centers in the 2027 budget, nearly twice this year's amount.

sections.title: Dating in the boom
sections.intro: The NYT finds SF founders running first dates like interviews and tracking conversion rates.

sections.title: The swarm papers
sections.intro: YC Labs publishes the multi-agent experiments behind yesterday's Minecraft story: emergent roles, hierarchies and coordination.

sections.title: Agents do the work
sections.intro: An agent drives stereotaxic arms for mouse brain surgery under a vet's kill switch, Better Together lets personal agents gang up on spam, and inside the frontier labs the agent workdays already outnumber the human ones.

sections.title: The alignment desk
sections.intro: Anthropic shows training data can be crafted to slip past production monitors, a poisoning paper plants an RCE backdoor with 0.1% of pretraining data, red-teamers find 11 ways around Codex's Auto-review, and Scott Alexander argues SURA has it wrong.

sections.title: The adoption question
sections.intro: The Census Bureau now asks about 'Super Intelligence,' and State of AI reminds everyone there is no single adoption rate to argue about.

sections.title: Anthropic's S-1
sections.intro: Q3 revenue near $17B, up 12x in a year, with the first profitable quarter in Q2 - and a headline loss that is mostly accounting.

sections.title: The labs' week
sections.intro: Mythos 5.5 leaks through Anthropic's own HTML, OpenAI merges Chat and Work (and the token pools), Rosalind-6 gets a trusted-access bio tier, and Musk calls Grok Bot unsustainably expensive.

sections.title: Rules of the road
sections.intro: Google backs a shared robots.txt policy token so sites can state training preferences once, across providers.

sections.title: The open-weight question
sections.intro: Startups surgically unlearn censorship out of Chinese models for Western buyers, while DeepSeek publishes its Super-Agent prototype with honest disclaimers.

sections.title: The abuse economy
sections.intro: WIRED finds a 400-domain network of mundane-looking apps that flip into deepfake generators, running on Apple, Google and Meta at once.

sections.title: The agent shopper, measured
sections.intro: DoorDash counts the agent-commerce revolution so far: several hundred orders, against 3 million deliveries a day.

sections.title: The research shelf
sections.intro: A hundred trained weights wake skills no prompt can reach, and humans& trains a tutor model against a simulated student.

sections.title: Pray for chaos
sections.intro: geohot picks his apocalypse: chaos over order, because order is the cage.

sections.title: The hardware horizon
sections.intro: Apple is reportedly building a $1,000 tabletop robot for 2027-2028.
